# terminal_graphics_interactive

> Keyboard and mouse input for terminal_graphics: build interactive terminal games, art, animations and drawing tools in Rust. Works in Windows PowerShell, Windows Terminal, Linux and macOS terminals, and over SSH. Its only dependency is terminal_graphics (re-exported), and the only `unsafe` is a few raw-mode calls.

It adds what `terminal_graphics` lacks: reading key presses and mouse events (click, drag, scroll). `Terminal::start()` switches to a full-screen session, `terminal.poll(timeout)` returns events and doubles as the frame timer, and `terminal.draw(&display)` shows a `Display` so that mouse positions line up with its cells. Everything from `terminal_graphics` is re-exported, so one dependency and one import is enough: `use terminal_graphics_interactive::prelude::*;` brings in `Display`, `Colour`, `Graphics`, `Container`, `Text`, `Rect` and `Ball` together with `Terminal`, `Event`, `Key`, `Mouse` and the rest.

Status: early (0.1) and not yet published to crates.io. Use it from git:

    terminal_graphics_interactive = { git = "https://github.com/calum/terminal_graphics_interactive" }

## Use it when

- You want a terminal program that reacts to the mouse or keyboard: a paint program, a game, a visualiser, a menu or a maths/physics toy.
- You want animation driven by input and a timer in one loop, with no async runtime and no other crates.
- You need it to behave the same in Windows PowerShell, Linux, macOS and over SSH.

## Do not use it when

- You only print output with no input. Use `terminal_graphics` alone.
- You need widgets, layout, text boxes or forms. Use a TUI framework.
- You need images in the terminal (Kitty, Sixel, iTerm2) or 24-bit colour. This is a grid of characters with the 16 ANSI colours.
- You need the program to keep running after the terminal closes, or to read from a pipe. `Terminal::start()` needs a real terminal.

## How it fits together

- `Terminal::start() -> io::Result<Terminal>`: enters the alternate screen, raw mode, mouse reporting and a hidden cursor, finds the window size, and reads input in the background. Dropping it restores everything, even on panic. It returns an error saying what to do if there is no terminal.
- `terminal.poll(timeout) -> io::Result<Option<Event>>`: waits up to `timeout`. `None` means the time ran out, which is the cue to advance an animation frame. `Duration::ZERO` checks without waiting. `terminal.wait() -> io::Result<Event>` blocks until something happens.
- `terminal.size() -> (u32, u32)`: window size in cells as `(width, height)`; `(80, 24)` if the terminal did not answer.
- `terminal.draw(&display) -> io::Result<()>`: shows a `Display` at the top left of the window. Call it once per frame.
- `Event` is `Event::Key(Key)` or `Event::Mouse(Mouse)`.
- `Key` has `code: KeyCode` and `modifiers: Modifiers`; `key.is_char('q')` and `key.is_ctrl('c')` cover the common checks. `KeyCode` is `Char(char)`, `Enter`, `Tab`, `Backspace`, `Esc`, `Up`, `Down`, `Left`, `Right`, `Home`, `End`, `PageUp`, `PageDown`, `Insert`, `Delete` or `F(1..=12)`.
- `Mouse` has `kind: MouseKind`, `x`, `y` and `modifiers`. `MouseKind` is `Down(MouseButton)`, `Up(MouseButton)`, `Drag(MouseButton)`, `Moved`, `ScrollUp` or `ScrollDown`; `MouseButton` is `Left`, `Middle` or `Right`. `mouse.cell_in(&display) -> Option<(isize, isize)>` gives the display cell under the pointer, or `None` if it is outside.
- Lower level pieces are public too: `Parser` (`feed`, `next_event`, `flush`) turns input bytes into events, and `RawMode::enable()` is the raw-mode guard.

## Mistakes to avoid

- Ctrl+C does not stop the program while a `Terminal` exists. It arrives as a key event, so check `key.is_ctrl('c')` and leave your loop, or the user can only close the window.
- The display passed to `draw` must be at most one row shorter than the window height (`height - 1`) and no wider than the width, or it is drawn off screen.
- Mouse coordinates are 0-based cells with `(0, 0)` at the top left, the same as `Display`. Do not subtract 1.
- Raw mode turns off the terminal's own newline handling. If you print lines yourself, use `\r\n`, not `\n`. Drawing with `draw` is unaffected.
- Run in a terminal. Over SSH use `ssh -t host command`, or `Terminal::start()` returns an error. Under tmux or screen, turn their `mouse` option on to receive mouse events.
- Not every terminal sends every event: `MouseKind::Moved` (movement with no button held) is not reported, only presses, releases, drags and scrolling.

## Example: click to mark cells, q to quit

This is `examples/quickstart.rs`, which cargo compiles, so it is known to build.

```rust
use std::time::Duration;
use terminal_graphics_interactive::{Colour, Display, Event, MouseKind, Terminal};

fn main() -> std::io::Result<()> {
    let mut terminal = Terminal::start()?;

    // `draw` needs a display at most one row shorter than the window
    let (width, height) = terminal.size();
    let mut display = Display::new(width, height.saturating_sub(1));

    loop {
        terminal.draw(&display)?;

        // wait up to 50 ms for input; `None` means a frame passed with no input
        match terminal.poll(Duration::from_millis(50))? {
            Some(Event::Key(key)) if key.is_char('q') || key.is_ctrl('c') => return Ok(()),
            Some(Event::Mouse(mouse)) if matches!(mouse.kind, MouseKind::Down(_)) => {
                if let Some((x, y)) = mouse.cell_in(&display) {
                    display.set_pixel(x, y, 'X', Colour::BrightYellow, Colour::Blue);
                }
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }
}
```

More examples: `cargo run --example paint` (a paint program), `cargo run --example screensaver` (bouncing dots with fading trails; shows the frame-timer loop: draw, handle input until the next frame is due, advance) and `cargo run --example events` (prints every event).
